Got Questions?

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Everything you need to know about Pro Wash™, Pro Detail™, and Pro Tint™ services.

Learn

UNDERSTANDING AUTO CARE

New to professional auto care? No worries. Here's what you need to know: straight talk, no fluff.

A hand car wash is when trained technicians wash your vehicle by hand. No machines, no spinning brushes. We use microfiber mitts, professional-grade soap, and clean water to carefully clean every surface. That means your body panels, wheels, tires, windows, door jambs, and all the tight spots automated washes completely miss. Hand washing provides a deeper, more detailed clean that protects your paint from swirl marks and micro-scratches, while keeping your car's value intact.
Car detailing is a deep cleaning and restoration of your vehicle, way beyond a regular wash. Think of it as a full reset. Interior detailing means deep vacuuming, steam cleaning carpets, conditioning leather, removing stains, and eliminating odors. Exterior detailing includes clay bar treatment, polishing, wax or sealant application, and paint correction. The goal is to make your car look and feel like it just came off the lot. A wash maintains your car; a detail restores it.
Window tinting is applying a thin film to the inside of your car windows. It blocks up to 99% of harmful UV rays, reduces heat by up to 60%, adds privacy and security, and gives your vehicle a sleek, customized look. Professional tinting with quality film won't bubble, peel, or turn purple like cheap DIY kits. Our installations come with a lifetime warranty. If it ever fails, we fix it free.
Hand washing provides superior, detailed cleaning that protects paint from swirl marks, while automated washes offer speed and convenience at lower costs. Brush-type automated washes can damage clear coats with micro-scratches over time. Hand washing is best for maintaining car value, protecting paint, and cleaning hard-to-reach areas like wheels and crevices. If you care about your car's long-term appearance and resale value, hand washing is the smarter choice, especially for luxury cars, ceramic coatings, and newer vehicles.
Most experts recommend washing every 2 weeks (or weekly if you park outside or drive a lot). For detailing, every 3-6 months keeps your interior and exterior in top condition. Regular care prevents dirt, road salt, bird droppings, and tree sap from permanently damaging your paint. Think of it like regular maintenance: consistent care prevents expensive problems down the road.

WHAT IS CAR DETAILING?

What is car detailing exactly?

Car detailing is a deep, thorough cleaning and restoration of your vehicle, way beyond a normal car wash. It involves meticulous cleaning, polishing, and protecting every surface inside and out. Interior detailing covers deep vacuuming, steam cleaning, leather conditioning, stain removal, and odor elimination. Exterior detailing includes clay bar treatment, polish, wax or sealant, and paint correction. The goal is to make your car look and feel like it just rolled off the lot.

What's the difference between a car wash and a detail?

A car wash cleans the surface: soap, rinse, dry, done in 20 minutes. A detail goes deep. We're talking about getting into every seam, vent, crevice, and fiber. Steam cleaning carpets, conditioning leather, removing water spots, polishing paint, and applying protective coatings. A wash maintains your car. A detail restores it. Most people need a wash every 2 weeks and a full detail every 3-6 months.

How long does a car detail take?

It depends on the package. An express detail takes about 45-60 minutes. A master detail can take 2-3 hours because we're covering everything: interior deep clean, exterior buff and wax, engine bay, the works. We complete all detail jobs between 8 AM and 4:30 PM so your car is ready same-day.

How often should I detail my car?

Every 3-6 months is ideal for most vehicles. If you have kids, pets, eat in your car, or park outside regularly, consider every 2-3 months. Regular detailing protects your interior from UV damage, keeps leather from cracking, maintains paint condition, and honestly, it just makes driving more enjoyable when your car is clean.

Is detailing worth the money?

Absolutely. A properly detailed car can add hundreds, sometimes thousands, to your resale value. Beyond money, it prevents long-term damage like cracked leather, faded paint, permanent stains, and musty odors. It's maintenance, not luxury. The same way you service your engine, you should service the surfaces you actually see and touch every day.

Can you detail my car at my home or office?

Yes! All of our detail packages are available as mobile service. We come to your home, office, or anywhere in the DMV area. There's just a $10 dispatch fee added to any service. Online booking not available for mobile — call customer service at (301) 307-1414 for an appointment.

WHAT IS A HAND CAR WASH?

What is a hand car wash?

A hand car wash is exactly what it sounds like. real people washing your car by hand, not machines. Our trained technicians use microfiber mitts, quality soap, and clean water to carefully wash every inch of your vehicle. That means your body panels, wheels, tires, windows, door jambs, mirrors, and all the spots automated washes completely miss. It's the safest, most thorough way to clean your vehicle without damaging the paint.

Hand wash vs. automatic car wash. what's the real difference?

Hand washing provides a deeper, more detailed clean that actually protects your paint from swirl marks and micro-scratches. Automated washes. especially brush-type. drag trapped dirt across your clear coat every time, dulling and damaging it over time. Hand washing is better for your wheels, crevices, trim, and overall vehicle value. Automatic washes are faster and cheaper, but if you care about maintaining your car's appearance and resale value, hand washing is the smarter choice. That's the trade-off: convenience vs. quality.

Is hand washing better for my car's paint?

Yes. Hand washing is the best option for protecting your car's paint, especially if you have a ceramic coating, wax protection, or a luxury/new vehicle. Soft mitts and careful technique mean zero swirl marks, zero brush scratches, and zero clear coat damage. How often should I wash my car?

Most experts recommend every 2 weeks, or weekly if you drive a lot, park outside, or live near heavy traffic. Regular washing prevents dirt, road salt, bird droppings, and tree sap from eating into your paint. Think of it like brushing your teeth. consistent care prevents expensive problems down the road. WHAT IS WINDOW TINTING?

What is window tinting?

Window tinting is the process of applying a thin film to the inside of your car's windows. This film reduces the amount of sunlight, UV rays, and heat that enters your vehicle. It also gives your car a sleek, customized look. Professional tinting uses high-quality film that won't bubble, peel, or turn purple over time, unlike cheap DIY kits.

Why should I tint my windows?

There are real practical reasons beyond looks. Tinting blocks up to 99% of harmful UV rays that cause skin damage and fade your interior. It reduces heat inside your car by up to 60%, so your AC works less and you stay comfortable. It adds privacy and security: people can't easily see your belongings inside. And in an accident, the film helps hold shattered glass together, adding a layer of safety.

Is window tinting legal in Maryland and DC?

Yes, with limits. In Maryland, front side windows must allow more than 35% of light in. Rear side and back windows can be any darkness. DC has similar rules. Our certified installers know the local laws and will help you choose a tint level that's legal, looks great, and gives you the protection you want. We don't want you getting pulled over.

How long does window tinting take?

Most tinting jobs are done in under 2 hours. A 2-window tint takes about 45 minutes, and a full vehicle (all windows) takes about 1.5-2 hours. Every tint job also includes a free car wash, so your car comes out looking fresh from every angle.

How long does window tint last?

With professional installation and quality film, window tint lasts for years, often the life of the vehicle. That's why we include a lifetime warranty on every installation. If it ever bubbles, peels, or discolors, we'll fix it at no charge. Cheap tint from an inexperienced installer? That might last a year before turning purple. You get what you pay for.

Can I roll down my windows right after tinting?

We recommend waiting 3-5 days before rolling down your newly tinted windows. The film needs time to fully cure and bond to the glass. You might also notice small water bubbles during the first few days, that's completely normal and they'll disappear as the tint cures. After that, your tint is set for life.
